Docs/Teleoperation

Teleoperation

Prepare a matched control and mirror setup, collect a staged episode, and review it before training.

From human motion to robot targets

The paper's collection setup uses a Quest 3 headset, MANUS Meta Gloves Pro and controllers mounted on the backs of the hands. Wrist tracking drives arm inverse kinematics; calibrated finger retargeting produces hand-joint targets. The simulator supplies visual feedback and task-success signals.

Choose a formal target from task/config/collection_targets.py. Match its task module, environment ID, robot UID and hand profile in the control and mirror processes. The canonical collection list has 10 complete tasks and 30 stages; legacy aliases are not additional collection targets.

Prepare the operator and runtime

Research checkout required

The module examples on this page require an asset-complete research checkout, its compatible Python environment, and the relevant simulator or model dependencies. The current public repository ↗ contains a README, license and repository metadata; cloning it does not provide the task modules, robot assets, datasets or checkpoints used below. These examples document the verified research interfaces.

  1. Verify the selected hand's SDK connection and the workstation's VR tracking before loading the task.
  2. Calibrate finger retargeting and verify left/right hand mapping, joint limits and wrist axes.
  3. Load the same environment and robot in the control and mirror processes, then confirm the shared workspace alignment.
  4. Use the launcher's --dry-run check to inspect environment, agent and joint wiring before collection.
  5. Test a short movement in simulation and confirm recording labels come from the environment's success predicate.

The dry run constructs the configured environment and checks wiring; it still needs simulator assets and a renderer. It is not an SDK-free public installation test.

Record to a pending store

With the bridge, VR feedback and task profile configured, the mouse stage uses the following research recorder interface:

python -m data_gen.teleop.manus_teleop \
  --task office_mouse --env-id SharpaAngledClickMouse-v1 \
  --robot-uids panda_sharpa_hand_right_angled_mobile_base \
  --arm-ik nullspace --wrist-control --vr-project --vr-project-qpos \
  --record --auto-segment --record-fps 20 --episode-seed 0 \
  --record-pending-dir data/teleop_pending

Add --dry-run to validate this launch without opening headset, glove or SDK connections. Actual collection also needs the calibrated operator profile and its matched mirror process. Use the task-specific launch profile for other targets. Review each pending episode and video before exporting it to the training dataset. Confirm the reset seed, task/source fingerprint and controller metadata, then run restoration and open-loop replay checks described in Data & replay.

Check bridges and hand profiles

The Sharpa bridge uses upstream port 2044 and downstream port 6668. Wuji and XHand have their own SDK, retargeting and runtime profiles. Inspect the selected hand's configuration before reusing another hand's launch arguments.

ss -ltnp '( sport = :2044 or sport = :6668 )'

If a bridge reports an address-in-use error, identify the existing listener and reuse it or close its owning terminal cleanly. Match both ends when changing a connection. SDK credentials belong in the local runtime setup and should not enter dataset exports or shared logs.

For policy-facing differences between hands, continue to Embodiments.
